name: Material & normal maps
oneLiner: A script turns every generated bitmap with alpha into a height map (alpha distance field rounded into a dome, plus the painting's own local light and dark as relief), a normal map (Sobel), ambient occlusion and a gloss mask, packed into one lossless file next to the picture with sha256 and the derive settings in the manifest (re-derived and compared by assetcheck); a small module then lights the sprite on a plain 2D canvas from wherever the game's lights are (lantern on the hero, lamps, glowing pickups), sharp at any scale and capped so it never washes out, and J-02 lights the same maps in WebGL.
fits: top-down action RPG and adventure with painted HD sprites
side-scrolling action / platformer with painted HD sprites
night, dusk, cave and dungeon scenes with lanterns, torches, spells
any HD game moving from code-drawn shapes to generated painted sprites (L-00) that should react to light
portraits and UI items that catch a highlight (busts, slots, potions, keys)
notFor: pixel-art styles (pixel8, pixel16, handheld4): a painted normal map on a 16 px sprite reads as noise
true 3D lighting with shadows cast by the sprites (the height is a 2.5D guess from a flat picture; use K-family 3D for that)
art whose light is baked in strongly (rim light, cast shadows painted in): it ends up lit twice; generate with even, neutral light
pages opened as file:// (pixels cannot be read: sprites draw unlit, nothing breaks)

needs: GameDNA_Assets (L-00 loader) loaded first; the game's boot moved into its onReady callback
the albedo picture and its <key>-nh map (nh2 layout) in the same manifest; tools/assets/normalmap.py to derive maps for new art
every draw site of the replaced characters / props: feet point, drawn height, facing
the game's light sources in the same coordinates as the draw calls (hero lantern, lamps, fires, glowing pickups, projectiles), from game state and the game clock
provides: nm.draw(ctx, key, x, y, {h, flip, alpha, lights, ambient}) -> bool: the sprite lit by up to 3 point lights + a key light, false only when the picture is missing
nm.maps(key) / nm.sample(key, x, y): decoded normal, height, occlusion, gloss (viewers, WebGL uploads for J-02)
tools/assets/normalmap.py derive / build / check / preview; assetcheck.py normalmap rule (re-derives and compares pixels)
assets.json: albedo (byte-identical to the L-00 / L-02 / L-06 packs) + one role normalmap entry per sprite with derivedFrom, params, albedoSha256 and sha256

promptParams.default: the character or prop the game draws most often (the hero if it is drawn at least 40 px tall)
chosen from the scene's mood (day 0.85, dusk 0.6, night 0.4)
a lantern on the hero plus every lamp, fire, glowing pickup or projectile the game draws
every character or prop of the game that one of the pack's pictures fits (pack prompt)

variants.name: Night village, keeper carries the lantern

assets: module/normal-maps.js: GameDNA_NormalMaps (one global, no dependencies; reads images through GameDNA_Assets from L-00)

assets/assets.json: 9 albedo files (8 byte-identical copies of L-00 herbalist, keeper, lamppost, well, vial, key; L-02 maren; L-06 slot; plus lamppost-off, one Codex edit with the lantern out) + 9 derived nh2 maps, 488 KB; assets/README.md describes the layout
assets/prompts/templates.md: style lock (even, neutral light), subject briefs, post-process + derive commands, light settings
tools/assets/normalmap.py (shared): derive, build, check, preview; assetcheck.py normalmap rule

assetPack.tool: codex image_gen.imagegen (built-in) for the albedo (L-00, L-02, L-06 runs, plus one edit run for lamppost-off); maps derived by tools/assets/normalmap.py
assetPack.check: tools/assets/assetcheck.py assets/assets.json (re-derives every map); checks/litcheck.py <run> (lighting wired in a game)
assetPack.regenerate: prompt.md + assets/prompts/templates.md + tools/assets (normalmap.py, postproc.py, assetcheck.py, namecheck.py)

related: art-direction-lock (L-00): loader and style-lock method; the sprites come from its pack
normal-lighting (J-02): lights the same nh2 maps in WebGL through I-08
dynamic-lights (J-01): its light list can drive this module when drawn in the same coordinates
